neutral_facts.value: The accused was prosecuted for the rape and murder of the victim. The victim, a young woman, went to a field to attend her goats and did not return home. Her father searched for her and found her dead with injuries on her chin and neck. The accused was identified as the perpetrator through the testimony of an eyewitness who claimed to have seen him and his accomplice commit the rape and murder. The accused was also found to have possessed items that were later linked to the crime. The prosecution relied on the eyewitness testimony, corroborative statements from the victim's family, and medical evidence indicating the cause of death was asphyxia due to throttling. The accused was initially sentenced to death for murder and life imprisonment for rape, but the High Court reduced the death sentence to life imprisonment and the life imprisonment to 7 years.

defence_argument.value: The accused contended that conviction could not have been based upon sole testimony of PW-1 as the same is not reliable. Also, the doctor's remarks that no mark of sexual violence was found on the genital organs of the deceased made the conviction under Section 376 unsustainable. The accused also argued that after the death sentence was commuted to life imprisonment, he should have been released after expiry of 14 years.
